701: C is correct because subscribing to AWS Shield Advanced provides managed DDoS protection for the public ALB endpoint and includes 24/7 access to the AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT), which proactively engages during attacks and integrates mitigating controls into the service with essentially no configuration changes to the application. DRT engagement reports, along with Shield Advanced health dashboards and Amazon CloudWatch metrics, provide visibility and an audit trail of attack sources and the mitigations applied. In contrast, WAF rule tuning or adding a CloudFront distribution requires more configuration and architectural change.
702: B is correct because the Snowball Edge devices import the 200 TB dataset into Amazon S3, and Amazon FSx for Lustre can integrate directly with that S3 bucket, presenting the data as a high-performance file system to the HPC cluster. FSx for Lustre is purpose-built for HPC workloads, delivering consistent sub-millisecond latencies and hundreds of GBps of throughput, exactly matching the requirement. Storage Gateway or EFS cannot provide that latency and throughput profile for HPC.
703: B is correct because AWS DataSync is designed to move data between on-premises NFS servers and Amazon S3, with a lightweight agent handling scheduled, incremental syncs of only changed data, making it the most cost-effective choice for periodic backups of small amounts of data. AWS Glue is an ETL service, AWS Transfer for SFTP incurs higher per-server costs, and Direct Connect is far too expensive for small periodic transfers.
704: C is correct because a Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4, supports UDP, and can handle millions of requests per second with ultra-low latency, making it ideal for game server traffic, and it preserves client source IP addresses. An ALB only supports HTTP and HTTPS at Layer 7, a Gateway Load Balancer is for inline security appliances, and duplicating game servers across Regions is not cost-effective.
705: A is correct because the migration is heterogeneous (RDS for MySQL to Aurora PostgreSQL), so AWS DMS Schema Conversion is required to transform database objects such as schemas, data types, and stored procedures into the PostgreSQL-compatible format. D is correct because a DMS task with change data capture (CDC) replicates the ongoing data changes that occur on the source during the migration to the target Aurora PostgreSQL cluster, keeping them in sync until cutover so no changes are lost.
706: B is correct because creating a read replica offloads the periodic reporting script's read queries from the primary instance so they no longer compete with the critical application, and it requires only the cost of one replica with no application redesign. Reading from instances with the fewest connections still hits the production writer, caching does not help ad hoc reporting queries and adds code changes, and manual daily exports create ongoing operational overhead.
707: B is correct because ALB access logging captures detailed records of every request into Amazon S3, and Amazon Athena can query those logs with standard SQL without any infrastructure to manage, giving the most operationally efficient visibility into the abnormal traffic access patterns. CloudTrail records control-plane API events rather than data-plane traffic patterns, while manually searching log files or using EMR is highly inefficient.
708: C is correct because public NAT gateways must be deployed in public subnets that have a route to an internet gateway, which enables them to translate and forward outbound traffic from the EC2 instances in the private subnets to the public internet while staying within the same VPC. Private NAT gateways are used to reach other VPCs or on-premises networks without public internet access, and NAT gateways cannot reside in the same private subnets as the instances whose traffic they serve.
709: B is correct because attaching the SCP directly to the three nonproduction member accounts applies the deny policy only to those accounts, blocking launches of the prohibited EC2 instance types exactly where required. E is correct because creating a dedicated OU, attaching the SCP to it, and moving the three nonproduction accounts into that OU scopes the policy to them through inheritance while leaving the production account unaffected in the root OU. Attaching the SCP to the root OU would also restrict the production account, and the management account is not affected by SCPs.
710: A is correct because a VPC gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 provides private connectivity between the EC2 instances and S3 over the AWS private network, and an S3 bucket policy that allows access only from that VPC endpoint enforces the restriction, keeping classified data traffic off the public internet. IAM policies and access keys control authorization but do not provide a private network path, and a NAT gateway still traverses the public internet.
711: C is correct because adding Aurora reader instances lets the cluster scale out to absorb the heavy read load, while Amazon RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections between the application and the cluster, reducing connection overhead and enabling fast, predictable failover with minimal downtime. EventBridge logging, zero-downtime restart, and DMS write-around caching do not add scalable read capacity or connection management.
712: A is correct because a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint, combined with a resolver rule associated with the VPC, securely forwards DNS queries from the VPC across the VPN to the on-premises DNS servers so instances can resolve private on-premises DNS records. An inbound endpoint solves the opposite problem of resolving AWS names from on-premises, and a private hosted zone only resolves records you host in Route 53 rather than names served by on-premises DNS.
713: B is correct because S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent and infrequent access tiers based on changing access patterns with no retrieval fees, which matches photos that are heavily viewed for months and others viewed for less than a week. Storing the photo metadata and its S3 location in DynamoDB provides fast single-digit millisecond lookups to determine which photos to display each user. DynamoDB is not suited for 20 MB photo objects, and Glacier or fixed 30-day lifecycle policies do not fit the unpredictable viewing durations.
714: B is correct because the least outstanding requests routing algorithm forwards each new request to the target with the fewest in-flight requests, so overloaded EC2 instances naturally stop receiving new requests until their queue drains, which directly addresses the observed imbalance. Round robin distributes requests evenly without regard to each instance's current load, so it would continue sending new traffic to already overloaded instances.
715: A is correct because AWS Budgets natively supports a Savings Plans coverage budget where you set a coverage threshold and it automatically sends notifications to the configured email recipients whenever Compute Savings Plans coverage drops below that level, using a fully managed service with no custom code. A Lambda function with SES requires custom development and maintenance, a budget report alone does not send threshold alerts, and a Savings Plans alert subscription does not provide configurable coverage threshold notifications.
716: A is correct because reusing the existing VPC and simply adding public subnets for the MSK cluster is the least disruptive, most operationally efficient way to make the cluster publicly reachable, and enabling mutual TLS authentication in the MSK security settings encrypts data in transit while authenticating both clients and brokers. Creating an entirely new VPC duplicates infrastructure and effort, and load balancers are not transparent proxies for Kafka's client-to-broker protocol.
717: D is correct because an internal Transfer Family SFTP server in two Availability Zones is reachable from the on-premises ERP system over the company's existing private connectivity, Amazon S3 provides durable and resilient storage, and a Transfer Family managed workflow invokes the Lambda function immediately upon file upload so orders are processed right away without hourly polling. This keeps the endpoint private, resilient across AZs, and event-driven, unlike internet-facing servers, EFS-based single-AZ options, or scheduled polling designs.
718: C is correct because AWS Outposts brings native AWS services and infrastructure into the on-premises data center, so migrating the Hadoop and Spark applications to Amazon EMR clusters on Outposts keeps all data processing on premises while AWS manages cluster provisioning and scaling, dramatically reducing operational complexity. The other options all copy or pull the data into the AWS cloud for processing, which violates the requirement to keep the processing on premises.
719: B is correct because Amazon FSx for ONTAP natively supports both SMB and NFS protocols for the Windows, Mac, and Linux EC2 instances, and its built-in auto-tiering moves infrequently accessed data from the fast SSD tier to the lower-cost capacity pool tier while keeping routinely accessed data on SSD, all within one managed file system. EFS does not support SMB, the S3 File Gateway adds appliance and protocol overhead, and FSx for OpenZFS does not provide multi-protocol SMB and NFS access.
720: C is correct because running the application on Amazon ECS as microservices decouples the tightly coupled modules so each can be deployed, patched, and scaled independently, and rolling deployments plus service auto scaling minimize downtime and let capacity flex with demand. A single Lambda function remains a monolith and cannot exceed the 15-minute timeout needed for 20-minute report generation, Spot Instances risk interruptions that force reports to restart, and Elastic Beanstalk's all-at-once deployment causes downtime on every patch.
